thread:
elaine: quick PSA — last night ~01:12 UTC we saw a spike of soft 429s from the prefetch-enabled GPU pool. not full outage but perf regressed 30% on tail. traces look like admit logic aggressively split high-KV-hit requests into tiny microbatches and then kernel sampler kept switching kernels mid-batch.
vikram: yikes. any specific kernel switch pattern? gptq -> fp16 thrash?
elaine: looks like sampler oscillated between small-window kernel (low-latency path) and large-batch kernel when a second request landed. visible in perf trace: kernel_hint=small -> assemble_batch(size=1) -> kernel_hint=large -> reassemble
kevin: can you paste the small snippet of logs? helps to see timestamps + events
elaine: sure
elaine: ```
2026-03-14T01:11:59Z [admit] req=0x7ffa size_est=512 kv_hit=true -> queued
2026-03-14T01:12:00Z [batch] assemble id=923 size=1 kernel_hint=small
2026-03-14T01:12:00Z [sampler] kernel_swap requested->large
2026-03-14T01:12:00Z [batch] reassemble id=923 size=1 -> no coalesce
2026-03-14T01:12:00Z [admit] soft-429 issued req=0x7ffa cause=budget-exhaustion
```
sam: that reassemble/no-coalesce line is suspicious — should be merging within 3ms window. sounds like admit window closed too early because token_budget target got hit by concurrent long seqs.
vikram: Could be our token-budget target math (target_per_gpu) being too conservative when prefetch boosts KV-hit probability. Prefetch reduces compute per-token but we still burn window quota. we need separate accounting for KV-hit savings.
kevin: idea: add quick-path token_credit boost for KV hits so admit doesn't punish coalescing. i.e., effective_token_cost = base_cost * kv_multiplier where kv_multiplier < 1.
elaine: agree. Also add a short inertia timer in sampler: once kernel_hint chosen for a batch, hold it for 6ms or until batch size crosses threshold. avoid flip-flopping on single arrivals. small change but likely big payoff.
ops-bot: perf-alert: soft-429-rate=6.2% (threshold 3.0%) @here
sam: actionable list?
elaine: 1) change token accounting for KV-hit requests (kv_multiplier = 0.6) 2) sampler sticky_timer = 6ms 3) admit: expand assemble window by +2ms when pool_kv_hit_rate > 30% 4) add debug histogram for reassemble events (count, time delta)
vikram: i'll own (1) and (3). plan to run canary on prefetch pool tonight with traffic replay.
kevin: i'll own (2) + histogram. adding unit tests for sampler sticky behavior. will also add a tracing tag to batch lifecycle to pinpoint reassemble causality.
sam: we should also document fallback policy: if sticky_timer causes >1% latency overhead on p50 for small requests, auto-roll back sticky_timer = 0. Config flag = runtime.admit.prefetch.sticky_ms
elaine: good call. also set canary parameters: ramp 5% -> 25% over 30m, monitor soft-429-rate, kernel-switch-rate, batch-coalesce-rate, and tokens-per-batch.
vikram: replay link: https://replay.internal/replay/2026-03-14/prefetch-burst (notes in replay)
kevin: quick PR draft in my branch kevin/kv-token-accounting. testing locally now.
elaine: if canary looks good we'll push to prod tomorrow morning and keep reassemble histogram for 24h. thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started for prefetch-pool at 2026-03-14T08:15:00Z (5% traffic)
sam: followups: post-mortem note in #postmortems if we see regression after change. add a short blurb to runbook about kernel-sampler sticky parameter.
elaine: noted. I'll open the runbook PR after we confirm canary metrics.
kevin: one more observation—when kernel swaps we should keep KV cache ownership tag on batch so we don't evict speculative KV entries unnecessarily. adding that to PR too.
elaine: perfect. closing loop. will post final canary metrics in this thread later.
